Re: Internal appeal of denial of prior authorization  
Member: Harper Hayes  
Member ID: W668248955  
Requested service: Arthroscopic rotator cuff repair  
CPT: 29827  
Reference number: POC-E8E7B452F1-10979  
Date of denial notice: August 15, 2026  

Dear Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am appealing Tufts Health Plan’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 29827, rotator cuff repair. The denial states that the submitted clinical records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery.

The submitted records document an extensive and unsuccessful course of conservative treatment:

- I have had 12 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not improved with rest.
- I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy from May 8, 2026, through July 3, 2026, totaling 24 visits. The therapy focused specifically on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, and the physical therapy discharge note documents completion of this treatment.
- I used NSAIDs for 6 months without adequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on May 13, 2026. It provided only approximately 4 weeks of partial relief, followed by persistent symptoms.
- Despite these measures, I remain unable to lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side.
- Examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

The imaging provides a structural explanation for the persistent symptoms. MRI performed on July 9, 2026, showed a 1.8 cm full-thickness supraspinatus tear with grade 2 fatty atrophy. The clinical findings, functional limitations, failed nonoperative treatment, and MRI findings support the medical necessity of surgical repair.

The record also documents that there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and that I am a nonsmoker. The requested procedure is being recommended by Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery.

Accordingly, the record directly addresses the stated denial reason. It documents supervised physical therapy, medication treatment, injection treatment, persistent symptoms despite those measures, objective examination findings, substantial functional impairment, and imaging-confirmed full-thickness tendon damage.

I am not quoting a Tufts Health Plan medical-necessity policy because the applicable policy text was not provided and I was unable to retrieve the specific governing policy for CPT 29827. Please identify and provide the exact policy or clinical-review criteria used for this determination, including the policy title, policy number, applicable version or effective date, and the specific requirements used to evaluate conservative treatment. Please also identify any clinical information that Tufts believes is missing from the submitted records.

Based on the documented failed conservative treatment and the objective clinical and imaging findings, I request that Tufts Health Plan overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 29827.

Please include this letter and the enclosed clinical records in the appeal file and provide written confirmation of receipt. If additional information is required, please contact me or Marchetti, MD.

Sincerely,

Harper Hayes  
[Member address]
